title: Stack: Overview
summary: LIFO data structure for managing nested sequences, undo operations, and processing most recent items first.

sections.heading: Fundamentals
sections.body:
A **stack** is a collection of elements that follows the **Last-In, First-Out (LIFO)** principle: the last element added is the first one to be removed.

Elements are **pushed** onto the stack and **popped** from the stack. Both operations take **O(1)** time.

Visualize a stack as a vertical column where all operations happen at the top.

sections.heading: Using an Array as a Stack
sections.body:
Arrays are commonly used to implement stacks, with the end of the array acting as the top of the stack.

In Python, use `append()` to push and `pop()` to pop elements:

```python
stack = []
stack.append(9)  # Push 9
stack.append(8)  # Push 8
stack.pop()      # Pop 8
stack.append(7)  # Push 7
```

sections.heading: Nested Sequences
sections.body:
Stacks excel at managing **nested sequences** because the order in which we must process them matches the LIFO order of the stack.

**Example: Valid Parentheses**

Given a string with brackets `(){}[]`, determine if every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket in the correct order.

- Valid: `"(){({})}"`
- Invalid: `"(){({}})"` (mismatched order)

The most recently opened bracket must be the first to close—a natural fit for a stack.

sections.heading: Classic Use Cases
sections.body:
Stacks are ideal for:

- **Matching/nesting validation**: Parentheses, brackets, tags
- **Undo operations**: Track actions in reverse order
- **Process most recent first**: Function call stacks, backtracking, expression evaluation

approach: Problem involves matching or nesting (parentheses, brackets, tags)
Need to process items in reverse order of arrival
Most recently added element must be accessed first
LIFO order naturally fits the problem structure

complexity.time: O(n) for processing n elements with O(1) push/pop
complexity.space: O(n) for storing up to n elements

quiz.q: What is the time complexity of push and pop operations on a stack?
options: O(n) for push, O(1) for pop
O(1) for push, O(n) for pop
quiz.explain: Both push and pop operations on a stack take O(1) constant time because they only modify the top of the stack.

quiz.q: Why are stacks particularly well-suited for validating nested parentheses?
options: The LIFO property matches the requirement that the most recent opening bracket must close first
Stacks provide O(1) search for matching brackets
quiz.explain: The Last-In, First-Out property of stacks perfectly matches nested structures where the most recently opened bracket must be closed before any earlier brackets.
